The shift

For every person in your company there are now 109 machine identities. AI agents are the fastest growing kind, and most of them hold more access than anyone has reviewed.

Life of an access request

An AI agent asks for access.
Five things should happen next.

agent://invoice-assistantrequesting
  1. 01

    Discover

    It's in the inventory, with a named owner and a purpose. No shadow agents.

  2. 02

    Authenticate

    Workload identity and a short-lived token. No API key pasted into a prompt.

  3. 03

    Authorize

    Least privilege, just in time. Read invoices, yes. Change bank details, no.

  4. 04

    Approve

    High-impact actions pause for a person, with the agent's intent in plain words.

  5. 05

    Audit

    Every call is logged against the agent and its owner, and reviewed like any other access.

        The playbook

        Six controls for agentic identity.

        1. 01

          Find every identity

          People, service accounts, API keys and agents, in one inventory.

        2. 02

          Give every agent an owner

          A named person answers for what it can do.

        3. 03

          Least privilege, just in time

          Access that is scoped, conditional and expires.

        4. 04

          No standing secrets

          Short-lived tokens. Vaulted, rotated keys.

        5. 05

          People approve high-impact actions

          Money, data exports and access changes pause for a human.

        6. 06

          Log it, review it, certify it

          Agents join the same access reviews as everyone else.
